entries.description: Register.
Remove the files and the code named in "What goes" above. Keep everything named in "What stays". The monolithic evidence path must behave exactly as it did before set 138 touched `verify.py`.

Confirm the accounting: the suite drops by 51 tests, and no import, CLI verb, or schema reference to the removed surface survives anywhere — including `ai_router/__init__.py`, the prompt templates, and the VS Code extension's command list.
Cross-provider verification.
Required portion of the full test suite.
Close-out.
Registered session 1 (copilot).

Deleted context_scope.py, pulls.schema.json and the two scope test modules; restored verify.py and ledger.py to their pre-138 state (the set-138 diff to both was purely additive scope work); removed declared_module_slug from session.py, keeping parse_set_config.

Suite drops 475 -> 424, exactly the 51 removed. No import, CLI verb, schema, doc or extension reference to context_scope/pulls survives; verify grant/refuse are rejected by argparse while dispute/adjudicate/waive and --transport are intact. PromptTooLargeError, parse_set_config and the modules.py manifest extension all remain.
Round 1 VERIFIED by gpt-5.5/openai over copilot-cli (orchestrator claude-opus-5/anthropic).

Full pytest suite green: 424 passed in 137s (475 before, minus the 51 removed), 56 slots free against the 480 ceiling. No suites are declared under testing.suites in router-config.yaml, so there is no separate test-evidence record to write.
Work committed (62340a19) and pushed; 5/5 close gates pass.
Register.

Apply the `session log` subcommand and its five tests from the salvage directory: a `log` verb on the existing `ai_router.session` CLI that resolves a step against the seeded plan rows, refuses an unresolvable key rather than appending an orphan row, enforces the closed status vocabulary at the boundary, and is idempotent.

Apply the two stale-doc corrections: `README.md` claims no shipped CLI exposes `--transport` (`ai_router.verify` does), and `docs/quick-start.md` describes bootstrap persisting `DABBLER_TRANSPORT` at system/HKLM scope (it is user scope by default, `--machine-scope` for the machine hive, with an announced fallback). Document `session log` in `quick-start.md` and `schema-reference.md`.

Consolidate the engine instruction files onto one source of truth. Verified against the vendors' own docs, 2026-08-19: Copilot CLI loads `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md` **and** `AGENTS.md` simultaneously whatever the model, and de-duplicates nothing — so today it ingests the shared managed body twice. Claude Code does **not** read `AGENTS.md` natively, and Gemini CLI does not either without a `context.fileName` opt-in, so a single file is not available. Both, however, expand an `@file` import inline at load time, and the `@AGENTS.md` import is Anthropic's own documented remedy for this exact case. - `AGENTS.md` carries the managed body. `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` carry `@AGENTS.md` plus their engine tail, and nothing else. - **Restore `GEMINI.md`.** v1 wrote all three engine files; the v2 rebuild's `write_instruction_files` writes only two, while the tail still claims Gemini reads `AGENTS.md`. `google` is a supported provider, so this is a live gap, not a tidy-up. - **Correct both tails.** Each currently asserts a per-engine file split that is false on Copilot. - No symlink. Anthropic endorses one, but it needs Developer Mode and `core.symlinks` on Windows, which is this repo's primary platform. - Out-of-fence user content stays untouched, as `render_engine_file` already guarantees.

Move this repo's own preamble from `CLAUDE.md` to `AGENTS.md`. The v2 ground rules — the test budget, "no new module without deleting one", the transport precedence — sit outside the fence in `CLAUDE.md` only, so a Codex session reading `AGENTS.md` never sees them. That is a correctness bug independent of the duplication, and it is why the body's new home must be `AGENTS.md` rather than the other way round.
Bump the version and build the artifact. Publishing itself is operator-gated: the session prepares the build and stops.
Cross-provider verification.
Required portion of the full test suite.
Close-out, and the end-of-set `change-log.md`.
Registered session 2 (copilot).

Applied the log subcommand from salvage (146 lines in session.py: _plan_rows_for, _resolve_plan_row, log, and the CLI verb) plus its 5 tests as TestLogCLI. 42 tests in test_session.py green. declared_module_slug deliberately not carried back.

README --transport claim and quick-start HKLM/user-scope claim corrected from salvage; session log documented in quick-start.md and schema-reference.md. The salvage's module-mapping, seven-tier and escalation doc sections were deliberately NOT applied -- they document the cancelled architecture.

bootstrap now writes three engine files: AGENTS.md carries the managed body, CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md carry the @AGENTS.md import plus their tail. GEMINI.md restored; both tails corrected. render_engine_file takes an optional body so the importing files share one code path.

Repo preamble (39 lines: v2 header, ground rules, environment) moved from CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md, so a Codex or Copilot session reading AGENTS.md now sees the ground rules. CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are 9 lines each, down from ~140.

Bumped 1.0.9 -> 1.1.0 (minor: new session log verb and a third instruction file are additive behaviour; the removed context_scope surface never reached PyPI, which still has 1.0.0). Built sdist + wheel: dabbler_ai_router-1.1.0-py3-none-any.whl (143 KB). Wheel carries no context_scope.py and no pulls.schema.json, and its bundled router-config.yaml still reads profile: api. Publishing remains operator-gated; not published.
Round 1 VERIFIED by gpt-5.5/openai over copilot-cli (orchestrator claude-opus-5/anthropic).
Full pytest suite green: 430 passed in 134s. 424 after session 1, plus the 5 session-log tests and 1 instruction-file test. 50 slots free against the 480 ceiling.
